Additionally, Guvacine Hydrochloride is also shown to target VMRC-LCP, which is a target of another compound, [4-(1,2,2-Trimethylcyclopentyl)phenyl]methanol, which also targets prostate cells. These findings collectively indicate that Guvacine Hydrochloride may exert its effects on prostate cells through the activation of VMRC-LCP, which is a common pathway in the context of prostate cell regulation. The evidence is consistent with a mechanism where Guvacine Hydrochloride influences prostate cell function via the VMRC-LCP pathway, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
